{"sourceType":"ESA Tender Action","sourceSystem":"ESA esa-star Publication","sourcePage":"https://esastar-publication-ext.sso.esa.int/ESATenderActions/filter/open","id":156240,"idEra":23245,"activityNumber":"1000043062","contractNumber":"","tanumber":"1-12813","title":"NAVISP-EL1-079 REDUCED SIZE ANTENNA FOR EARTH PULSAR NAVIGATION - EXPRO+","description":"Pulsars are rapidly rotating neutron stars emitting beams of radiation periodically, some with very high stability, emitting in all the spectrum (infrared, visible, RF, X-ray). Since every pulsar has a different frequency, they can be used in a navigation system like beacons, as well as in timing. For space navigation, detectors in X-ray are preferred due to the reduced size of the associated detectors, even though detectors in the visual range could also be used. On ground, RF detectors are preferred due to the strong absorption of X-rays in the atmosphere.
